## How the SOFAR Channel Carries Distant Whale Calls

The SOFAR channel is a naturally occurring pathway in the ocean through which low-frequency sound can travel long distances. Sound waves bend up and down through the channel, while a hydrophone positioned near its axis can detect sounds from far away, including whale calls.

In some instances, low-frequency sound can travel across entire ocean basins. The channel’s sound-carrying behavior helps explain how distant whale calls can reach a hydrophone.
